transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I came in today because... well, I've just been having a bit of a hard time lately. I guess I keep feeling like I’ve really let my family down by taking on this mortgage. It's probably just me overthinking things, right? But it’s gotten to where every small mistake I make at work—I wait tables right now—it just feels like it proves I’m completely useless. Like I just deserve whatever bad things happen to me. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds a little dramatic to start off with. Is that... is that the kind of thing you needed to know?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, it's been a while, I suppose. Maybe... about a year and eight months? Yeah, it started right around the time I took on the mortgage for the condo. 

I mean, I'm sure it's normal to be a little stressed about money, right? A lot of people have mortgages. I just... I guess I haven't been handling it as well as I should be. I hope that's an okay answer? I just don't want to make a bigger deal out of it than it actually is.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends or family?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I still really like doing the things I usually do. I mean, waiting tables takes up a lot of my time and energy, but when I have a day off, I still enjoy seeing my friends or... or going over to see my family. 

I haven't really lost interest in any of that. I always try to make an effort to be good company for everyone, you know? I hope that's a good sign. Is it... is it okay that I still enjoy those things even though I've been feeling so down about everything else? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed that you feel tired or lacking in energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?

Um, tired? No, I wouldn't say I feel tired most days. I mean, waiting tables can be pretty exhausting, especially when it's a busy shift, but... but that's just normal tired, right? Like anyone would feel after working on their feet all day. 

When I'm just at home or not doing much, I feel fine. I usually have plenty of energy to get things done around the condo or run errands. I'm definitely not just sitting around feeling wiped out all the time. I try to stay as active as I can. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that right.
Have you ever felt so overwhelmed or down that you've thought about hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?

Oh, gosh, no. I mean, I definitely don't have any sort of plan to hurt myself or anything like that. I promise I would never do that. 

But, um... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... sometimes when I'm lying awake before an early shift at the restaurant, I do get these thoughts. Just... thinking that maybe it would be easier if I just didn't wake up, so I wouldn't have to keep feeling like I'm failing at everything. 

But it's really just a passing thought, you know? I don't actually want to do anything bad. I think it's just the stress talking. Is that... is that a normal thing to feel sometimes when you're overwhelmed? I really hope I'm not alarming you by saying that, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture.
Have you been feeling like you’re a failure or that you’ve let people down more often than usual, even if it might not be entirely your fault?

Um... well... I guess I have been feeling a little bit like that, yeah. But I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining or feeling sorry for myself. 

It's just... that's actually kind of why I came in. I've been feeling so bad about the condo. Like, I took on this mortgage, and I just keep thinking I've completely let my family down by doing it. And then at work, if I mess up an order or drop something, it just... it feels like it proves I'm completely useless, you know? Like I just deserve whatever bad things happen to me. 

But I know I shouldn't think that way, and I'm really trying to stay positive. I just... I don't want you to think I'm a negative person or anything. Is it normal to feel that guilty over things like a mortgage or a small mistake at work? I hope it's okay that I shared that with you.
Have you been feeling guilty or like you’re not good enough most days, even when things aren’t entirely your fault?

Um, yeah, I guess that's sort of exactly what I was just trying to say. I hope I wasn't repeating myself too much. 

But yes, that's really the main reason I decided to come in. I just... I keep having this overwhelming feeling that I've completely let my family down by taking on this mortgage. And it spills over into everything else, too. Like, if I drop a glass at the restaurant or mess up a table's order, it just feels like this huge proof that I'm completely useless. Like I just deserve whatever bad things happen. 

I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself, and I really do try to be a good employee and a good person. I just... I hope it's okay that I feel that way sometimes. Is it pretty common for people to get stuck feeling guilty like that? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right so you have what you need.
Have you ever had periods in the past where you felt down or guilty like this for more than two weeks at a time?

Um, well... I guess I have, yeah. I mean, I really don't want to sound like I've just been moping around forever, because I do try my best to keep a smile on at work and be pleasant for the customers. 

But, um... if I'm thinking back, these feelings—like the being down and the guilt over the condo and everything—it's actually been going on for a while. I'd say maybe... about a year and two months? Give or take? 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a lost cause or anything. I really have been trying to push through it and not let it bother anyone else. Is it... is it okay that it's been going on for that long before I came in to see you? I just didn't want to be a bother until it felt like I really couldn't shake it.
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt down or struggled with guilt like this for at least two weeks?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I've always tried to be a pretty upbeat person, you know? I really like making sure people have a good time when they come into the restaurant, so I usually try to keep things light and positive. 

Before all this started with the condo... I don't really remember ever feeling this bad for that long. I mean, sure, everyone has a bad day here and there, right? But nothing like this where it just kind of... sticks around for weeks and weeks. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, maybe it means this is just a bump in the road and I can get back to my normal self soon? I just... I really want to be back to being the kind of person who doesn't drag everyone else down. Does that make sense?

Have you ever had a period in your life before this one where you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks, not counting times when you were just reacting to a big event like a breakup or losing a job?

Um, no, I really don't think so. I mean, I hope I'm answering this right, because you asked something similar just a minute ago, right? I'm sorry if I'm making you repeat yourself, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

But yeah, before this whole thing started, I really was doing okay. I mean, I've always been the kind of guy who just rolls with the punches, you know? Even if something stressful happened, I'd usually just bounce back after a few days. I never really had a time where I felt this... this down for weeks on end. 

I try really hard to be a positive person, and I'd hate to think I've been secretly depressed my whole life or something. So, no, nothing like this before the condo stuff. I hope that's the right answer? Like, I hope that helps you figure out what's going on with me.
Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period when you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Um, I'm really sorry, I know you're trying to be thorough, and I feel like I keep giving you the same answer. I really hope I'm not frustrating you! 

But yeah, it's just this current stretch that's been like this. For the past year or so, most days there's just this... this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I still go into work and carry the plates and make sure I smile for everyone, but it feels like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I do it because I'm supposed to, not because I'm actually feeling anything good inside. 

Before this started, I really never felt that way. I was genuinely happy to be at work and be around people. I hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself a little bit. I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know. Am I doing okay with these questions?

Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period when you experienced a major depressive episode — meaning you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, and it significantly affected your daily life for more than two weeks?

Oh, gosh, I'm so sorry... I feel like I'm failing a test or not explaining myself right, since we keep coming back to this same question. I really don't mean to be difficult! 

But honestly, no, never before this current time. Like I was just saying a second ago, it's really only been lately that I've had that... that heavy, empty feeling sitting in my chest most days. Where I'm just putting on my work smile and carrying the plates because I'm supposed to, not because I actually feel anything good inside. 

But before all this started? No, never anything like that. I was always a pretty happy, upbeat guy before this. I hope I'm finally answering that the way you need me to? I just really want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you the right information for your notes.
Have you ever had a period in your life before this one where you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, for more than two weeks in a row?

Oh, wow, I... I am so sorry. I feel like I'm really messing this up for you, since you have to keep asking me the same thing over and over. I promise I'm not trying to hide anything or be difficult! I just... I really want to be a good patient and give you the answers you need. 

But, um, to answer your question again... no, never before this current time. It's just been this past year or so where I've had this... this heavy, empty feeling sitting right here in my chest most days. I still go to work, I still carry the plates and put on a smile for the customers, but it's just... I'm just going through the motions because I know I'm supposed to, not because I actually feel anything good inside anymore. 

But before this? No, I swear, I was totally fine. I was always a pretty happy guy. I hope that's what you were asking? Am I... am I doing okay with these questions? I really hope I'm not making your job harder.
Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period when you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, for more than two weeks in a row?

Oh my gosh... I am so, so sorry. I must be doing a really terrible job explaining myself, or maybe I'm completely misunderstanding what you're asking? I feel awful making you repeat this again, I promise I'm trying my absolute best to give you what you need! 

But, um... no. Never before this current stretch. It's really just been lately that I've had that heavy, empty feeling in my chest most days. Before this, I never felt like I was just going through the motions, you know? Like carrying the plates and forcing a smile just because I'm supposed to, without feeling anything good inside. That's all new. I used to be totally fine before this started. 

Am I... is there a specific way I should be answering this? I just really want to make sure I'm doing this right for you.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking again about periods of feeling down most of the day, nearly every day, which corresponds to Depressed Mood.

patient.answer:
Oh my gosh... I am so, so sorry. I must be doing a really terrible job explaining myself, or maybe I'm completely misunderstanding what you're asking? I feel awful making you repeat this again, I promise I'm trying my absolute best to give you what you need! 

But, um... no. Never before this current stretch. It's really just been lately that I've had that heavy, empty feeling in my chest most days. Before this, I never felt like I was just going through the motions, you know? Like carrying the plates and forcing a smile just because I'm supposed to, without feeling anything good inside. That's all new. I used to be totally fine before this started. 

Am I... is there a specific way I should be answering this? I just really want to make sure I'm doing this right for you.

opening_question.intent: Greet the patient and identify the primary reason for the visit
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has experienced a single, continuous major depressive episode lasting over one year, with no prior history of major depressive episodes, which supports the diagnosis of persistent (dysthymic) major depressive disorder.
